questions.question: The impression of an image persists on the retina for about _________ of a second.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1/16th.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• This feature is called** persistence of vision**.
 
• Due to this, when many still images are shown in a sequence; they give the illusion of moving images.
 
• Persistence of vision is the capacity of the eye to maintain an image on the retina for a moment after the image has disappeared.
 
• This is due to a prolonged chemical reaction.
 
• As a result, the eye cannot clearly distinguish changes in light that occur faster than this retention period.
 
• The changes either go unnoticed or they appear to be one continuous picture to the human observer.
 
• If successive images follow quickly enough, these will be perceived as a single continuously moving image.
 
• Animation, motion pictures or films, make use of persistence of vision to create the illusion of movement.
 
• Films consist of a series of still images (frames) that capture the progress of a subject in motion.

questions.question: "Population control and family planning" is listed in the _________ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.solution: The Constitution divides various items on which law can be made by relevant government in India under 7th Schedule. Laws on items in Union, State and Concurrent list can be made by Central, State and both governments respectively.

questions.question: _______ is issued when the court finds that a particular office holder is not doing legal duty and thereby is infringing on the right of an individual.
questions.solution:

‘Mandamus’ is a judicial remedy in the form of an order from a superior court to any public authority, to do some specific act which that body is obliged under law to do.

questions.question: Which of the following is an award given by the Government of India to recognize outstanding achievement in National sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arjuna Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Arjuna Award is the second-highest sporting honour in India, the highest being the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award.
 
• It is given by the President of India.
 
• The selection of candidates is done by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
• The awards are presented by the President of India in the same ceremony at the Presidential Palace, usually on 29 August.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ashok Chakra Class-III was renamed the Shaurya Chakra in 1967.

 
 
• The medal was originally established on 4 January 1952 as the "Ashoka Chakra, Class I".
 
• As the first step of a three-class sequence of non-combatant bravery decorations.
 
• In 1967, these decorations were removed from the "class-based" system and renamed as the Ashoka Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra. 
 
• The Ashoka Chakra is India's highest peacetime military decoration awarded for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the battlefield.
 
• Flt. Lt. Suhas Biswas was the first Indian Air Force officer to be awarded the Ashoka Chakra.
 
• A recipient can be awarded the Kirti Chakra or Shaurya Chakra in addition for separate acts of gallantry.
 
 
 
• The Dadasaheb Phalke Awards is India's highest award in cinema.
 
 
• This award is given annually at the National Films Awards.
 
• The very first recipient of this award was Devika Rani who received it in 1969 on the occasion of the 17th National Films Awards.
 
• Dadasaheb Phalke is known as the 'Father of Indian Cinema'.
 
• The first recipient of this award was Devika Rani. 
 
• The award comprises of a Swarna Kamal, a Cash Prize of Rs. 10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs)certificate, silk scroll and a shawl.
 
 
 
• About Padma Awards :
 
 
• The Padma Awards are announced annually.
 
• It was instituted in 1954, except for brief interruption (suspended) during the years 1978 and 1979 and 1993 to 1997.
 
• It is one of the highest civilian honors of India.
 
• A higher category of Padma award can be conferred on a person only where a period of at least five years has elapsed since the conferment of the earlier Padma award.
 
 
 
• Objective:
 
 
• It seeks to recognize achievements in all fields of activities or disciplines where an element of public service is involved.
 
 
 
• Disciplines:
 
 
• The Awards are given in various disciplines/ fields of activities, viz.- art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, civil service, etc.

questions.question: The material carried by the glacier such as rocks big and small, sand and silt gets deposited, which are called glacial ________.
questions.solution: Moraines are formed from debris previously carried along by a glacier and normally consist of somewhat rounded particles ranging in size from large boulders to minute glacial flour.

questions.question: _________ are defined as the mass movement of rock, debris or earth down a slope.
questions.solution:
A landslide is any geologic process in which gravity causes rock, soil, artificial fill or a combination of the three to move down a slope. 

Causes of Landslide

 
• slow weathering of rocks
 
• soil erosion,
 
• earthquakes
 
• volcanic activity

questions.question: Asterias (Star fish), Echinus (Sea urchin), Antedon (Sea Lily) are all examples of which Phylum?
questions.solution: Echinoderms (members of Echinodermata) are able to reproduce asexually and regenerate tissue, organs, and limbs; in some cases, they can undergo complete regeneration from a single limb.

questions.question: During uniform motion of an object along a straight line, the ________ remains constant with time.
questions.solution: Velocity is the representation of rate of motion with direction which remains constant with time in a uniform motion along straight line because it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, irrespective of the length of the time.

questions.question: Based on the common features like presence of notochord and dorsal hollow neural system, animals like fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds along with mammals are included in which Phylum?
questions.solution: Chordata phylum consists of animals called ‘chordates’. Chordates possess a notochord, a hollow dorsal nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, an endostyle, and a post-anal tail, for at least some period of their life cycle, for example glass catfish.

questions.question: A few organisms can tolerate and thrive in a narrow range of temperatures. Such organisms are called _________.
questions.solution: A stenotherm is a species or living organism only capable of living or surviving within a narrow temperature range. The opposite is a eurytherm, an organism that can function at a wide range of different body temperatures.

questions.question: The demand for an inferior good increase with ________ in the consumer's income.
questions.solution: Inferior goods are those goods that are graded low in terms of their utility amongst customers and therefore, when the income decreases their demand increases.
